errors.english: When examining the nature of the pervasion [note: the relationship between the logical reason and the property to be proven] and the pervader
errors.why: khyab par bya ba is the pervaded (vyāpya), paired with the pervader (vyāpaka); the text examines only the pervaded–pervader relation between the two vipakṣa terms, not 'the pervasion'.

fix.find: When examining the nature of the pervasion [note: the relationship between the logical reason and the property to be proven] and the pervader
fix.replace: When examining only the relation of the pervaded and the pervader

errors.english: even when being "not without a self" is reversed
errors.why: The Tibetan says that even when selflessness is excluded, the positive entity (the self) is not thereby established; the English makes the excluded term 'not without a self', i.e. the opposite.

errors.english: [note: referring to both the subject and the example]
errors.why: gnyi ga la grub pa med pa means the self is not established for both parties to the debate (proponent and opponent), not 'subject and example'.

note: Follows the kevalavyatirekin argument broadly, but the pervaded/pervader vocabulary and a couple of glosses are off, so a Pramāṇa reader would need to rework the logic passages.

errors.english: "Aha! You have established a meaning that was difficult to understand,"
errors.why: The bodhisattva does not think 'I have established a difficult meaning'; bdag gis is first person.

note: A sound rendering of the commentary on the teacher's qualities and the sūtra list of speech qualities, with one first/second person slip.
Careful 84000-style translation of the Saṃdhinirmocana commentary on name and basis; faithful throughout.
Accurate rendering of the refutation of manifestation/transformation as grounds for distinguishing cause and effect.
Faithful to the commentary on wisdom, method and consecration; inline glosses are clutter but not wrong.

errors.english: Depart out of fear at his mere command,
errors.why: In context of summoning all buddhas by the vajra finger-snap, gshegs means they come (assemble) at his command, not depart.

fix.find: Depart out of fear at his mere command,
fix.replace: Come, awed, at his mere command,

note: Generally sound for the wrathful-manifestation passage, but the first verse inverts the summoning (come vs depart).

errors.why: ye shes is gnosis/wisdom (jñāna), not faith.

errors.english: "May all merits, such as generosity, become concordant causes and may my generosity become inexhaustible."
errors.why: The purpose clause (so that all merits yield results concordant with their cause) is outside the dedication, whose words are 'may giving become distinguished and inexhaustible'; 'distinguished' is lost.

note: Good rendering of the Buddhānusmṛti commentary apart from 'faith' for ye shes and a reshuffled dedication formula.
Faithful rendering of the transition to the chapter on practice and the five special objects of training.

errors.english: because of what the twice-born (dvija) a member of the brahmin caste thought while oppressed by hunger, I am like a withered tree by the roadside
errors.why: The verse (Skt. dvijanmanā cintitaḥ kṣutparītena) says the king has been thought of / turned to by a hungry brahmin at the wrong time, like a dry tree on the road; the brahmin's thought is not the cause of his state.

note: The bilingual jātaka verses are rendered sensibly from the Tibetan; one clause misconstrues who thinks of whom.

errors.why: bu gcig ma is the mother of an only child (the image of undistracted care), not the child.

errors.english: Does not liberate because the self is not bound here.
errors.why: The Tibetan asks 'Listen, son, what are you conceptualizing?' and gives the reason that here the self is neither bound nor freed.

note: A reasonable verse translation of the doha-style instructions, with a few misconstrued similes and clauses.
